chapter: La Vida and Handy's own bands
title: Living with Tom Albert and his wife
summary: He lived in Albert's house; he tells of moving furniture for drinks and of Albert's wife Louise, who saved money.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: When you moved to the city, where did you live? What neighborhood?

I lived on Dauphin and St. Louis. Right with Tom Albert, right in his house with his wife. His little girl. They were same as my people. I lived right there with them. Go out and then we moved from there to Rightways Living. How about that? 635 Bagan Street. Right around the corner. We moved from there and we didn't have no truck either. Got everything around there by hand. He had a gallon of whiskey. And a clothes basket of sandwiches. And everybody we seen on the street. You want a drink? Yeah. Come on. Go get a piece of furniture and bring it around. We give you a drink. That's the way we moved. Everybody seen on the street thought they'd drink. They'd offer them a drink but they had to bring a piece of furniture for us before they get a drink. They had to give him a drink. They had a fine wife. They had a fine wife. Miss Louise was a very fine woman. Miss Louise was a very fine woman.
She's dead now? She's dead now?

Yeah, she's dead poor soul. She made Tom what he used to do. Because Tom used to work out there on the riverfront. Then he used to be a trapper. In the wintertime he'd do a lot of trapping and he made a lot of money. But if he'd leave him keeping, he'd throw it away.

And she'd taken that money and bought that house. She got it right there down. And uh, furnished it off. And when she died, she left him, she left him a lot of money. I don't know if he still got it, but she, I'd say a lot, she left him about twelve, fourteen thousand dollars. And she died. And he don't have to spend that money because he got everything in that house.
